curiosities: Steve Wozniak insisted on eight expansion slots, against Steve Jobs's wish for two.
VisiCalc, the first spreadsheet program, came out on the Apple II in 1979.
Jordan Mechner made Karateka and Prince of Persia on the Apple II.
The Apple IIe stayed on sale until 1993.
Its processor is a MOS 6502 at about 1 MHz.
It showed colour graphics, rare in a home computer then.
Wozniak's Disk II floppy drive of 1978 used remarkably few chips.
Wozniak wrote its first BASIC; Applesoft BASIC, licensed from Microsoft, replaced it.
Its moulded plastic case was unusual at a time of metal and wooden ones.
Richard Garriott's Ultima and Doug Smith's Lode Runner began on it.
The compact Apple IIc of 1984 could be carried with a handle.
The Apple II family sold around six million machines.
